method_problems: bag+graph is not a frozen prediction file. The plan's file gnn_opt/preds/eval/hgb_bag+graph.csv (like hgb_clock.csv and oracle_risk+clock.csv) holds night_val only, so its held-out scores were refit after the fact. The clock refit is exact: committed val and CV predictions are reproduced (CV after %.5g rounding). The bag+graph refit is a different model instance: night_val AUROC 0.9009 vs committed 0.9022 (max diff 0.104), and my local CV refit differs from the committed CV file by up to 0.176. bag+graph is the reference in 5 of the 11 primary tests (a1, b1, b2, b3, b6). The analyst disclosed this, and the likely AUROC effect is about 0.002 (their tab_mem refit check) against CI half-widths of 0.025-0.05, so no verdict changes. The paper should still call bag+graph 'refit on night_train for the held-out splits', not frozen.

For bag+graph, the threshold and the held-out scores come from different model instances. The threshold 0.1363 comes from the committed CV file (the GNN team's instance), while the scores come from the local refit, whose own CV would give 0.1411. The effect is nil here: recall is 0.276 at both thresholds and held-out FPR 0.048 vs 0.047.

The decision rule is cited from an older plan version. The report cites 'ANALYSIS_PLAN.md §4 / §4b', applies '>= 3/4 split signs' as plan criterion 2 and mentions a CV-CI criterion 1. The current plan (v2, /Users/mauricio/sim_local/apart_vx/ANALYSIS_PLAN.md, 19:05) has no §4b. Its rule is Holm p < 0.05 on the pooled held-out rows only, and split signs are reported for description. No verdict changes because no Holm p < 0.05, but phrases such as 'the sign criterion fails (2/4)' for a4, a5, b1 and b6 should be dropped or recast as descriptive. v2 is also untracked: git shows no commit, although it says it applies once committed. Its own §0 records that the held-out comparison was computed (19:00) before v2 was written, so the analysis is confirmatory, not blind, as v2 itself states.

The gnn5 and hybrid thresholds come from the GNN team's 4-run CV proxy, not the 5-seed final model; I verified that cv/cloud_final_gnn.csv equals e_ngru_4runs.csv exactly. Realised held-out row FPRs are 0.054 and 0.063, and across the primary set they span 0.029-0.063. R@5%FPR and lead-time comparisons are therefore not at equal FPR. This is disclosed and does not affect the AUROC family.

Some reported values depend on the bootstrap draws. The Holm p of 0.781 for a1/b2/b3 and the smallest Holm p of 0.090 come from one seed. With independent draws (seed 777, B=10,000) I get 0.720 and 0.084; the verdict of 0 of 11 significant holds. The two-sided percentile-bootstrap p uses 36 clusters, only 23 of which hold a positive, so it may be somewhat anti-conservative, as disclosed. That cannot create a significant result here.

A property of the plan's design, not an analysis error: the pre-registered rounds-to-cut bins leave absolute time informative. The clock scores 0.716 within these bins vs 0.530 with round bins, and the RQ2 verdict flips between the two definitions. The analyst reports both correctly. The paper must say that the primary (a) family tests the monitors against a strong clock.

Minor: the within-mixed statistic counts 9 mixed configs. Three of them are night_branch configs whose outcomes differ because their arms received different interventions, so they are not replicates of one setup. The harness schema (control arms only) lists 6. The statistic is secondary and partly disclosed.
